audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition numerator and denominator describe different businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,829.9 million consideration and $2,358.5 million net acquisition cash outflow; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-acquisition 2025 OE anchor excludes Soleno while the cash bridge and fully diluted shares reflect the post-acquisition company.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to our independent efforts to develop and market products, we may enter into collaboration and license agreements or acquire businesses from time-to-time to enhance our drug development and commercial capabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch reasonably capable of changing value. The bridge reflects cash spent to acquire Soleno, but operating value omits VYKAT XR. Soleno contributed $54.4 million of revenue from May 18 through June 30, 2026, and the filing provides combined pro-forma results. The acquisition was all-cash, so acquisition-related seller-share dilution is not demonstrated, but the numerator-versus-bridge inconsistency remains material.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized combined-company OE using the filed pro-forma and post-closing results, excluding transaction costs, accelerated compensation, purchase-accounting amortization and inventory step-up effects as appropriate; then rerun with June 30 cash, securities, debt and a consistently dated diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor contains a temporary zero-cost CRENESSITY inventory benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated CRENESSITY cost of revenues temporarily increases the 2025 OE anchor and every projected cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: In future periods, we expect to incur a higher cost of revenues that includes the cost of CRENESSITY active pharmaceutical ingredients produced following FDA approval.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary benefit is demonstrated: the filing states that CRENESSITY inventory included API with no cost basis and that 2025 cost of revenues excluded pre-approval manufacturing costs. CRENESSITY generated $301.2 million of 2025 sales, but the record does not identify the zero-basis inventory consumed or its steady-state replacement cost. Materiality therefore cannot be established, although the error can only reduce normalized OE and value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain quantities and post-approval unit costs for CRENESSITY inventory sold in 2025, normalize cost of revenues without re-expensing manufacturing costs already charged to R&D, and rerun all scenarios from the corrected anchor.

audit_findings.title: Large milestone obligations are not captured by a smooth owner-earnings growth path
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $15.35 billion of filed contingent milestone obligations as of June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Future milestone cash payments reduce OE in the periods triggered, but the DCF applies smooth growth without separately charging those payments.
audit_findings.evidence: With respect to our existing collaboration and license agreements, we may be required to make potential future payments of up to $14.87 billion upon the achievement of certain milestones.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are contingent rather than present liabilities, but their filed maximum is approximately 2.3 to 3.5 times the modeled $4.349-$6.557 billion equity values. Historical payments of $65.4 million in 2025 and $22.9 million in the first half of 2026 also demonstrate that milestones are recurring economic events, not merely boilerplate exposure. If pipeline success supplies forecast growth, omitting the associated probability-weighted payments can materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Map milestones, including acquired Soleno obligations, to every product contributing to scenario growth; assign filing-supported timing and probabilities, calculate after-tax cash costs, and rerun each scenario with those discrete payments.

audit_findings.title: Third parties retain profit-sharing and royalty claims on pipeline economics
audit_findings.magnitude: 50% of U.S. GBA1 operating profits and losses if Voyager exercises its opt-in; other royalty effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Profit shares, royalties, co-development costs and milestones reduce the portion of future product economics attributable to NBIX common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Voyager may elect to exercise such rights, pursuant to which we and Voyager would equally share in the operating profits and losses of such products in the U.S. (in lieu of Voyager being entitled to receive potential future payments of certain event-based milestones upon their achievement in the U.S. and receive royalties on the future net sales of such products in the U.S.), following Voyager’s receipt of the top-line data from a first clinical trial in Parkinson’s disease.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual claims are demonstrated, but the cited Voyager products are pre-commercial and the valuation does not identify any growth assigned to them. They are therefore forward-looking rather than a presently measurable error in the $372.0 million historical OE anchor. They would overstate value if future scenario growth credits gross product economics instead of NBIX's contractual net share.
audit_findings.action: Monitor program progress and, before attributing growth to any licensed product, model NBIX's net economics after the filed 50% profit share or applicable royalties, milestones and co-development obligations.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may omit noncurrent marketable securities
audit_findings.magnitude: $91.9 million, equal to $0.80 per diluted share, 1.6% of base equity value, and $0.56 per share after the 30% margin of safety
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted noncurrent available-for-sale securities belong in the nonoperating asset bridge because their investment income was removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We maintain a diversified investment portfolio consisting of low-risk, investment-grade debt securities with maturities of up to three years, including investments in commercial paper, securities of government-sponsored entities and corporate bonds that are subject to interest rate risk.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: $389.8 million equals June 30 cash of $332.4 million plus current securities of $57.4 million, while filed noncurrent securities of $91.9 million were omitted. Adding them raises base value from $49.07 to approximately $49.87 per share and buy-below from $34.35 to approximately $34.91. That scale cannot alter the conclusion relative to the $155.64 market price.
audit_findings.action: Add the filed $91.9 million of noncurrent available-for-sale securities to every scenario's bridge after confirming none are restricted or operationally committed; increase each value per share by approximately $0.80.

audit_findings.title: Disposed-business earnings may be projected alongside the sale proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: $63.2 million actual proceeds and $28.6 million pre-tax sale gain; recurring disposed-business OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 anchor contains the disposed unit's operating results, while the June 2026 cash bridge includes sale proceeds; retaining positive recurring OE would overstate value, while removing a recurring loss would increase value.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to December 31, 2025, on January 21, 2026, we completed the sale of Neurocrine Group Limited to Immedica Pharma AB for $ 65.0 million in cash, and we expect to recognize the related gain in the first quarter of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter inconsistency is demonstrated because the disposal was not presented as discontinued operations and 2025 results remain consolidated. However, the filings do not isolate the unit's recurring after-tax OE, so direction and materiality cannot be established. The proceeds discrepancy is resolved by the later filing: $65.0 million was the previously announced consideration, while $63.2 million was the actual cash received at closing.
audit_findings.action: Extract the disposed unit's 2025 revenue, operating costs, working-capital investment, maintenance capital expenditure and tax effects; remove its normalized recurring OE from the anchor, exclude the $28.6 million sale gain from OE, retain only the actual $63.2 million proceeds in the bridge, and rerun all scenarios.
